member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.Annotation
member.summary: Provides an base class for an annotation.
member.remarks:
Use an annotation to highlight a point or region of interest on a graph. An annotation consists of a caption that labels the annotation, an arrow pointing to the item of interest, and a shape highlighting the item of interest.
You can configure the appearance of the caption in several ways. Use the , , , and properties to change the text, color, and font used to display the caption. To configure the location of the caption, use the property. You can also configure the property to specify the angle of rotation in which the caption is drawn. Use the property to draw a caption above or below the plot data of the graph.
You can configure the appearance of the arrow by setting the , , , , and properties. Use the and properties to change the shape of the head and tail of the arrow. Use to draw the arrow above or below the plot data of the graph.

member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode
member.summary: Specifies the scaling mode of the specified axis.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.Fixed
member.summary: The axis fixes the range to the existing range. The range is never updated.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.AutoScaleLoose
member.summary: The axis automatically updates the range so that the range extends beyond the exact calculated data values.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.AutoScaleExact
member.summary: The axis automatically updates the range to the exact calculated values.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.ScopeChart
member.summary: The axis updates the range to behave as a scope chart. For example, if the existing range is 0 to 10 and a data value of 13 is plotted, the range is updated to 10 to 20.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.StripChart
member.summary: The axis updates the range to behave as a strip chart by scrolling to the most recent data value. For example, if the existing range is 0 to 10 and a data value of 13 is plotted, the range is updated to 3 to 13.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.AutoScaleVisibleLoose
member.summary: The axis automatically updates the range so that the range extends beyond the exact calculated data values for the subset of data in the range of the corresponding axis in the other dimension.

remarks.para: and are updated after the other axis is scaled in order to calculate the correct subset of data made visible by the other axis. When using an AutoScaleVisible on both axes, the horizontal axis is scaled before the vertical axis.
remarks.note:
You should use and in combination with , , or
to highlight a subset of the graph. When used with or , the AutoScaleVisible modes have the same behavior as the AutoScale modes since the entire graph is visible. However, since the AutoScaleVisible modes require additional computation to determine the visible region, performance decreases.

member.name: F:NationalInstruments.UI.AxisMode.AutoScaleVisibleExact
member.summary: The axis automatically updates the range to the exact calculated values for the subset of data in the range of the corresponding axis in the other dimension.

remarks.para: and are updated after the other axis is scaled in order to calculate the correct subset of data made visible by the other axis. When using an AutoScaleVisible on both axes, the horizontal axis is scaled before the vertical axis.
remarks.note:
You should use and in combination with , , or
to highlight a subset of the graph. When used with or , the AutoScaleVisible modes have the same behavior as the AutoScale modes since the entire graph is visible. However, since the AutoScaleVisible modes require additional computation to determine the visible region, performance decreases.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.BoundsAlignment.Auto
member.summary: Gets a bounds alignment that auto-aligns an item to the specified bounds.
member.value: A that auto-aligns an item to the specified bounds.

remarks.para: alignment places the item in one of nine locations: bottom left, bottom center, bottom right, middle left, middle center, middle right, top left, top center, or top right. The position of the item is determined by the shortest Euclidean distance between the item and the .

Annotations, for example, can use the property to auto-align the caption of the annotation. In the context of an annotation, the is the actual position of the annotation, the is the size of the caption, the is the plot area bounds, and the and are the annotation caption offsets.

The following figure shows how the property works. The items, which are the captions in the case of an annotation, are placed in the nine positions previously mentioned. The Euclidean distance from the the middle of the blue ellipseto the top left corner of each item is calculated. The position with the shortest distance is then chosen for the item. For example, in the following figure, the bottom center position would be chosen for the item and so the item would be placed there. If this example were an annotation, the caption would be placed in the bottom center of the plot area, and the and of the annotation would be applied from that position.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.ColorScale
member.summary: Represents the third axis on an intensity graph, where a value corresponds to a color.

remarks.para: The properties that affect the mapping are , , , , , and . The property defines the range of the . The and properties define the colors to use for values at the boundaries of and outside the range. The property defines a collection of objects, which are pairs of values and colors that determine how to map data values to color entries. The property determines how to calculate the color for values without an entry. The property determines whether the interpolation is linear or logarithmic. The following steps explain the process of mapping a value to color:

item.description: If the value is greater than , the value maps to .
If the value is less than , the value maps to .
If the value is in range and there is a object for the value, then the value maps to the color of the object.

If the value is in range and there is no object for the value, then one of the following occurs: If is , the value maps to the color of the with the value that is lower and nearest to the given value. If , the color is calculated by taking a weighted mean of the colors associated with the color map entry values immediately above and below the value. The weighted average is calculated linearly or logarithmically, depending on the property.

remarks.para: You can place the horizontally, at the top or bottom of the plot area, or vertically, at the left or right of the plot area. The default position is .
returns the bounds of the , and returns the size of the .
draws the color scale, and alters the spacing of the tick marks.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.ColorScale.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.remarks: A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.ColorGenerator
member.summary: Provides an base class for assigning different colors to multiple plots in the Windows and Web Forms scatter, waveform, and complex graphs.
member.example:
You can implement a custom color generator, as shown in the following example.
Public Class RandomColorGenerator Inherits ColorGenerator
Private _colors As Color()
Public Sub New() Me.New(8) End Sub
Public Sub New(ByVal numberOfColors As Integer) If (numberOfColors <= 0) Then Throw New Exception("Invalid parameter.") End If
Dim rand As New Random() ReDim _colors(numberOfColors - 1)
Dim i As Integer For i = 0 To numberOfColors - 1 _colors(i) = Color.FromArgb(rand.Next() Mod 255, rand.Next() Mod 255, rand.Next() Mod 255) Next i End Sub
Public Overrides Function GetColor(ByVal index As Integer) As Color Return _colors(Math.Abs(index Mod _colors.Length)) End Function End Class

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.IntensityRangeAnnotation
member.summary: Represents an annotation that highlights a range of values.

remarks.para: Use an to highlight a range on a graph. A range annotation enhances an annotation by adding properties that configure the drawing of the range. To specify the range of interest, set the and properties.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexAxis.InteractionMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the user interactions that are supported by the axis.
member.value: A that indicates which user interactions are supported by the axis. The default value is .
member.exception: The specified value is not a value.

remarks.para: Set the Enabled property to on the control containing the axis to enable interaction with the axis . If the Enabled property is , the has no effect regardless of its value. Also, the axis must be visible in order for the to have any effect.

If is set to , a user can interactively set the minimum and maximum values of the axis at run time. If the minimum value is set to a value greater than or equal to the maximum value, then the maximum value is set to the value obtained by adding the new minimum value and the old range interval. The axis then appears to slide in the positive direction. Similarly, if the maximum value is set to a value less than the minimum value, then the minimum value is set to the value obtained by subtracting the old range interval from the new maximum value. The axis then appears to slide in the negative direction.

For example, if the axis range is 10 to 30, the range interval is 20, calculated from 30 10. If the minimum value of 10 is interactively changed to 30, then the maximum value is changed to 50, calculated from 30 + 20. The new range is 30 to 50. Similarly, given an axis range of 10 to 30, if you change the maximum value from 30 to 10 interactively, then the minimum value is changed to 10, calculated from 10 20.

remarks.para: You can set this property to any instance of , including the format modes that the static methods return and any custom class that implements the base class.
The following format modes are available through the class:

item.description: Displays the value using a basic numeric format with a specified precision. Use the method to create an instance of a SimpleDouble format mode.
Displays the value using standard numeric format strings supported by . Use the method to create an instance of a Generic format mode.
Displays the value using standard engineering notations supported by . Use the method to create an instance of an Engineering format mode.
Displays the value using hexadecimal format. Use the method to create an instance of a Hexadecimal format mode.
Displays the value using binary format. Use the method to create an instance of a Binary format mode.
Displays the value using scientific notation format. Use the method to create an instance of a Scientific format mode.

remarks.para: For more information, refer to the class.
For formatting modes such as Generic and Engineering, the value displayed for editing differs from the formatted value, so the user does not see the formatted value until the control loses focus.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexCursor.LabelFormatString
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string that is used to format the label.
member.value: The format string that is used to format the label. The default value is "{R:N:G5}+{I:N:G5}i".
member.remarks:
The format string can be a combination of tokens and plain strings. The tokens are specified inside braces. A token should take the following form:
{TokenValue:FormatCategory:Format}
The "TokenValue" placeholder can take the following 4 values:
R - for real value
I - for imaginary value
M - for magnitude value
P - for phase value
The "FormatCategory" placeholder can take the following 2 values:
N - for numeric formats
E - for engineering formats
The "Format" placeholder can take any of the standard format specifiers.
The above tokens can be combined with plain strings also. Some of the valid FormatStrings and the resultant strings after formatting the complex value 5+6i are:
FormatString After formatting
"Magnitude = {M:E:ee} and Phase = {P:E:ee}"
"Magnitude = 7.810e+0 and Phase = 876.058e-3"
"{I:N:G5}i + {R:E:EE0}"
"6i + 5E+0"
"{{ R={R:N:G5}, I={I:N:G5}, M={M:N:G5}, P={P:N:G5} }}"
"{ R=5, I=6, M=7.8102, P=0.87606 }"
The braces in the plain string should be escaped manually. This is shown in the third FormatString example.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexCursor.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of with set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexPlot.ToolTipFormatString
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string that is used to format the tool tip.
member.value: The format string that is used to format the tool tip. The default value is "{R:N:G5}+{I:N:G5}i".
member.remarks:
The format string can be a combination of tokens and plain strings. The tokens are specified inside braces. A token should take the following form:
{TokenValue:FormatCategory:Format}
The "TokenValue" placeholder can take the following 4 values
R - for real value
I - for imaginary value
M - for magnitude value
P - for phase value
The "FormatCategory" placeholder can take the following 2 values
N - for numeric formats
E - for engineering formats
The "Format" placeholder can take any of the standard format specifiers.
The above tokens can be combined with plain strings also. Some of the valid FormatStrings and the resultant strings after formatting the complex value 5+6i are:
FormatString After formatting
"Magnitude = {M:E:ee} and Phase = {P:E:ee}"
"Magnitude = 7.810e+0 and Phase = 876.058e-3"
"{I:N:G5}i + {R:E:EE0}"
"6i + 5E+0"
"{{ R={R:N:G5}, I={I:N:G5}, M={M:N:G5}, P={P:N:G5} }}"
"{ R=5, I=6, M=7.8102, P=0.87606 }"
The braces in the plain string should be escaped manually (shown above in the third FormatString).
You can use this property only in Windows Forms projects.
member.exception: The format string is not well formed.

member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of with and set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexPointAnnotation
member.summary: Represents an annotation for a (x, y) data point.

remarks.para: Use a to highlight a point on a graph. A point annotation enhances an annotation by adding properties that configure the shape drawn around the point of interest. To specify the point of interest, set the property.

You can customize the appearance of a point annotation in many ways. Use the , , , , , and properties to change the color and style of the fill area as well as the color, width, and style of the bounding line. Use the property to specify the style of the shape displayed at the point of interest. Use the property to rotate the shape to a desired angle. Use the property to draw the shape above or below the plot data on the graph.
Use the property to completely hide all parts of the annotation when the point of interest is not located inside the plot area bounds.

The and events support custom-drawn point annotations. Use these events to participate in the drawing of the point annotation. occurs before the is drawn. occurs after the point annotation has been drawn.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexPointAnnotation.ToolTipFormatString
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string that is used to format the tool tip.
member.value: The format string that is used to format the tool tip. The default value is "{R:N:G5}+{I:N:G5}i".
member.remarks:
The format string can be a combination of tokens and plain strings. The tokens are specified inside braces. A token should take the following form:
{TokenValue:FormatCategory:Format}
The "TokenValue" placeholder can take the following 4 values
R - for real value
I - for imaginary value
M - for magnitude value
P - for phase value
The "FormatCategory" placeholder can take the following 2 values
N - for numeric formats
E - for engineering formats
The "Format" placeholder can take any of the standard format specifiers.
The above tokens can be combined with plain strings also. Some of the valid FormatStrings and the resultant strings after formatting the complex value 5+6i are:
FormatString After formatting
"Magnitude = {M:E:ee} and Phase = {P:E:ee}"
"Magnitude = 7.810e+0 and Phase = 876.058e-3"
"{I:N:G5}i + {R:E:EE0}"
"6i + 5E+0"
"{{ R={R:N:G5}, I={I:N:G5}, M={M:N:G5}, P={P:N:G5} }}"
"{ R=5, I=6, M=7.8102, P=0.87606 }"
The braces in the plain string should be escaped manually (shown above in the third FormatString).
You can use this property only in Windows Forms projects.
member.exception: The format string is not well formed.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexRangeAnnotation
member.summary: Represents an annotation that highlights a range of values.

remarks.para: Use a to highlight a range on a graph. A range annotation enhances an annotation by adding properties that configure the drawing of the range. To specify the range of interest, set the and properties.

You can configure the range appearance in many ways. Use the , , , , and properties to change the color and style used to fill the range as well as the color, style, and width of the line surrounding the range. Use the property to draw the range above or below the plot data on the graph. Use the property to specify where the arrow head is positioned on the range.
Use the property to completely hide all parts of the annotation when the range of interest is not located inside the plot area bounds.

The and events support custom-drawn range annotations. Use these events to participate in the drawing of the range annotation. occurs before the is drawn. occurs after the range annotation has been drawn.

If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.ComplexErrorDataMode
member.summary: Provides an class that defines a set of methods used for generating error data for a .

remarks.para: The class provides static methods for creating instances of the following common error data modes:

item.description: Generates no error data. Use the method to create an instance of a None error data mode.
Generates error data that is offset from plotted data points by a constant amount. Use the method to create an instance of a Constant error data mode.
Generates error data that is offset from plotted data points by a percentage of the values for the plotted data. Use the method to create an instance of a Percent error data mode.

remarks.para: The format of the string used to display symmetric error data modes in the designer is [mode name]: [symmetric offset], and the format used to display asymmetric error data modes in the designer is [mode name]: +[high offset], -[low offset].
remarks.note: When you implement a class that derives from , you must implement the method. You must also validate arguments of this method and handle invalid arguments appropriately.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.DigitalSignalPlot.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.DigitalWaveformPlot.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of . A deep copy of the is also performed.
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.FormatString
member.summary: Represents the format specifier and format provider to use to create a formatted string for a numeric value.

remarks.para: Use to specify a format specifier and format provider. The property contains the standard or custom format specifier to use to format a value. If the format string mode is , the format can be any valid format that is supported by . If the format string mode is , the format can be any valid format that is supported by . If the format string mode is , the format can be any valid format that is supported by . If the format string mode is , the format can be any valid standard or custom elapsed time format. Refer to Using Elapsed Time Formats with Measurement Studio Windows Forms Controls or Using Elapsed Time Formats with Measurement Studio Web Forms Controls for information about valid standard and custom elapsed time formats. indicates the format provider to use with the specifier.
You can override if you want to format values in ways that are not supported by format strings, such as scaling.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to format the labels of the major divisions of an axis to display numeric values with three decimal places.
Private Sub SetupAxis(ByVal targetAxis As Axis) targetAxis.MajorDivisions.LabelFormat = New FormatString(FormatStringMode.Numeric, "F3") End Sub

The next example demonstrates how to create a -derived class and override the method to create a custom scaling format where all values are multiplied by a fixed number when they are formatted.
Class CustomFormatString Inherits FormatString Private scalingFactor As Integer Public Sub New(ByVal scale As Integer) MyBase.New(FormatStringMode.Numeric, "G5") scalingFactor = scale End Sub Public Overrides Function FormatDouble(ByVal value As Double) As String Return MyBase.FormatDouble(value * scalingFactor) End Function End Class

example.note: Measurement Studio objects are immutable, meaning the object always returns the same string for a given input value. In some cases, assuming that these objects are immutable, Measurement Studio controls that use objects optimize during the paint cycle. If you have a class derived from that can return different output strings for the same input value, and you change the properties or fields of the derived class object, you might not immediately see the updates. National Instruments recommends you design the class derived from so that objects you create exhibit the same behavior throughout their lifetime. When you need to change a behavior, you create a new object and assign it to the control, rather than change the behavior of an existing object. In the previous example, if you want to change the scalingFactor used by the CustomFormatString object, create a new object of type CustomFormatString by passing in the new value for scalingFactor.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.IComplexGraph
member.summary: Defines the interface for graphs that plot data values.

remarks.para: You can use the collection to include multiple instances on a single graph. With multiple plots, you can plot multiple sets of data in the same plot area.

Use to plot the imaginary part against the real part of the or an array of imaginary values against an array of real values. plots imaginary values against real values by appending the values to the existing data.

and collections allow multiple x and y axes to coexist on a single complex graph. You can use multiple axes to plot multiple sets of data that are scaled differently from each other. The event occurs when the collection is modified through an add, remove, insert, or clear operation. The event occurs when the collection is similarly modified.
raises the event when the on a , contained in its collection, changes. Similarly, occurs when the on a , contained in its collection, changes.

Custom drawn plots are supported through the and events. occurs before the plot is drawn. occurs after the plot is drawn. Use these events to participate in the drawing of a plot that is contained in the plot collection. occurs when a new set of data is plotted.

Plot area cursors are supported. You can use cursors to annotate plots and the plot area. accepts multiple cursors through the collection. The event occurs when the collection is modified through an add, remove, insert, or clear operation.

member.remarks:
A value less than 1.0 indicates a zoom out, and a value greater than 1.0 indicates a zoom in. For example, a value of 0.8 zooms out by 80% and value of 1.5 zooms in by 150%. If is set to 1.0, the plot area is not zoomed because a value of 1.0 zooms by 100% of the view.
The imaginary and real parts of are mapped to client coordinates using the and properties, respectively, of . and act as the scale for mapping. The client coordinates are mapped to virtual coordinates using . The virtual coordinates are used to call .

member.summary: Defines the interface for all graph controls.
member.remarks:
defines the interface for all graph controls. Use a graph control to visualize data in a plot area.
supports multiple plots on a single graph. Use multiple plots to plot multiple sets of data in the same plot area. occurs when the collection of plots is modified through an add, remove, insert, or clear operation.
Use to clear data from all of the plots in the graph plot collection.
, , and provide the ability to change the appearance of the plot area. To retrieve the bounds of the plot area, use . Custom drawing of the plot area is supported through the and events. occurs before the plot area is drawn. occurs after the plot area is drawn. , , and provide a convenient way to draw the plot area image, grid lines, and plot area components, such as plots and cursors, while custom drawing the plot area. You can use these events to participate in the drawing of the plot area.
You can use and to zoom into the plot area around a point or a selection. pans the plot area relative to the existing view. can undo the last zoom or pan operation. reverts all zoom and pan operations to restore the plot area to its initial state.
The client coordinates of the plot area differ from the actual coordinates to enhance ease of use. You must use the bounds of the plot area in virtual coordinates when passing arguments to , , and . The virtual coordinates of the plot area are defined from (0.0, 0.0) to (1.0, 1.0). and convert client coordinates to virtual coordinates. and convert virtual coordinates to client coordinates.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.IGraph.PanXY(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Pans the plot area according to the specified horizontal and vertical factors.
member.param: The horizontal factor.
The vertical factor.
member.remarks:
If you set to 0.0, the plot area is not panned horizontally. If you set to 0.0, the plot area is not panned vertically.
An of 1.0 pans the plot area to the right so that the right edge of the plot area becomes the left edge of the plot area. An of -1.0 pans the plot area to the left so that the left edge of the plot area becomes the right edge of the plot area.
A of 1.0 pans the plot area to the top so that the top edge of the plot area becomes the bottom edge of the plot area. A of -1.0 pans the plot area to the bottom so that the bottom edge of the plot area becomes the top edge of the plot area.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.IntensityAxis.InteractionMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the user interactions that are supported by the axis.
member.value: A that indicates which user interactions are supported by the axis. The default value is .
member.exception: The specified value is not a value.

remarks.para: Set the Enabled property to on the control containing the axis to enable interaction with the axis . If the Enabled property is , the has no effect regardless of its value. Also, the axis must be visible in order for the to have any effect.

If is set to , a user can interactively set the minimum and maximum values of the axis at run time. If the minimum value is set to a value greater than or equal to the maximum value, then the maximum value is set to the value obtained by adding the new minimum value and the old range interval. The axis then appears to slide in the positive direction. Similarly, if the maximum value is set to a value less than the minimum value, then the minimum value is set to the value obtained by subtracting the old range interval from the new maximum value. The axis then appears to slide in the negative direction.

For example, if the axis range is 10 to 30, the range interval is 20, calculated from 30 10. If the minimum value of 10 is interactively changed to 30, then the maximum value is changed to 50, calculated from 30 + 20. The new range is 30 to 50. Similarly, given an axis range of 10 to 30, if you change the maximum value from 30 to 10 interactively, then the minimum value is changed to 10, calculated from 10 20.

The following format modes are available through the class:

Displays the value using standard numeric format strings supported by . Use the method to create an instance of a Generic format mode.
Displays the value using standard engineering notations supported by . Use the method to create an instance of an Engineering format mode.
Displays the value using hexadecimal format. Use the method to create an instance of a Hexadecimal format mode.
Displays the value using binary format. Use the method to create an instance of a Binary format mode.
Displays the value using scientific notation format. Use the method to create an instance of a Scientific format mode.

remarks.para: For more information, refer to the class.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.IntensityCursor.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of with set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.IntensityPlot
member.summary: Defines a class for plotting three-dimensional data on a two-dimensional surface where color represents the third dimension.
member.remarks:
An intensity plot is defined as a set of data represented by rectangular blocks of color on a coordinate system.
The intensity plot accepts data as a two-dimensional rectangular array of values. Each value in the array is drawn as a rectangular color block. The values along with the determine the of the rectangular blocks. The indices along with the start and increment values determine the position and size of the rectangular block.
Set to to calculate values for each pixel by interpolation and draw the plot pixel by pixel. This will result in a better view of the data, particularly if the size of the input data is small; however, interpolation could decrease performance.
You use method overloads which accept the xStart, xIncrement, yStart and yIncrement parameters to determine the starting position of the first rectagular block and the size of the rectangular blocks. For example, a rectanglular block with indices i, j in the input two-dimensional rectangular array will be drawn centered at (xStart + i * xIncrement, yStart + j * yIncrement) with width of xIncrement and height of yIncrement. If you do not define xStart, xIncrement, yStart and yIncrement, the values of , , and are used.
You can use and for charting in horizontal and vertical directions, respectively.
and determine the maximum number of data points in the horizontal and vertical directions that can store in history. History capacities are are applicable only during charting. and are the number of data points in the horizontal and vertical directions that are actually in history. Only data points stored in history are displayed.

and define the x-axis and y-axis used to scale the plot data. These values must not be when data is plotted. Use and to specify if the plot data is used to calculate the range of and , respectively.

Use with custom drawn plots to limit the data that is used for drawing only to those values that are visible in the current and ranges. Use after calling to transform the clipped x and y data to drawing coordinates.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.IntensityPlot.SmoothUpdates
member.summary: Gets or sets the value which specifies whether the plot is drawn to an off-screen buffer before drawing to the screen.
member.value: if a plot is drawn to an off-screen buffer before drawing to the screen. The default value is .

remarks.para:
Smooth updating improves performance in the following ways:
Eliminates flashing associated with plotting large plots.
Optimizes speed when you use graph cursors.
Optimizes speed when a graph is redrawn after it has been overlapped or hidden.

Smooth updating has the following disadvantages:
Plots slower because the plot is first drawn to an off-screen buffer and then drawn to the screen.
Uses extra memory for the off-screen buffer.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.IntensityYAxis.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.remarks: A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.INumericValueSource
member.summary: Defines the interface for all Measurement Studio controls that function as a numeric value source.
member.remarks:
Controls that implement this interface, such as the knob and tank controls, act as a source for a control that uses the interface, such as the numeric edit control. If the numeric edit source is set and its value is changed, it calls either the , , or methods to change the value of the source control. This way, changes to the numeric edit control are automatically reflected in controls that implement this interface, such as the knob or tank controls.
Raise the event before the value of the source control changes, and raise the event after the source control value is changed. The value can change when either , , or are called. Raise the event when the source control has been disposed. These events are useful for controls, such as the numeric edit control, that use this interface. For example, if the value of the source control, such as a knob, changes because the pointer was dragged, the numeric edit uses the and events to update its value. This way, the source and numeric edit control always have the same value.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.IScatterGraph
member.summary: Defines the interface for graphs that accept both x and y data values.
member.remarks:
The ability to specify x and y data values allows you to plot non-monotonically increasing data.
You can use the collection to include multiple instances on a single graph. With multiple plots, you can plot multiple sets of data in the same plot area.
Use to plot a single y value against a single x value or an array of y values against an array of x values. plots y values against x values by appending the x and y values to the existing data.
You can plot multiple sets of y data values against a single set of x data values with a single method invocation. Use to plot a 2D array of y values against an array of x values. behaves in much the same way, except that it appends the data to the existing data for plotting. plots a 2D array of x values against an array of y values. behaves similarly but appends the data to the existing data.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.IWaveformGraph
member.summary: Defines the interface for graphs that accept data as a waveform.

remarks.para: A waveform is defined as a set of data against equally spaced increments.
You can use the collection to include multiple instances on a single graph. With multiple plots, you can plot multiple sets of data in the same plot area.

Use to plot a single x value or an array of x values against a starting y value. uses the specified value to increment y values or a default value if one is not specified. plots x values by appending the values to the existing data.

You can plot multiple sets of x data values with a single method invocation. Use to plot a 2D array of x values against a starting y value. uses the specified value to increment y values or a default value if one is not specified. behaves in much the same way, except that it appends the data to the existing data for plotting.

member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of with and set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

You can configure the circle appearance in many ways. Use the , , and properties to change the the color, style, and width of the circle. Use the property to draw the circle above or below the plot data on the graph. Use the property to specify where the arrow head is positioned on the circle.

member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of the with the and set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: T:NationalInstruments.UI.NumericFormatMode
member.summary: Provides an base class that defines a set of methods used to format and validate numeric values.

remarks.para: The class provides static methods for creating instances of the following common formatting modes:

item.description: Displays the value using a basic numeric format with a specified precision. Use the method to create an instance of a SimpleDouble format mode.
Displays the value using standard numeric format strings supported by . Use the method to create an instance of a Generic format mode.

Displays the value using standard engineering notations supported by . Use the
method to create an instance of an Engineering format mode.
Displays the value using hexadecimal format. Use the method to create an instance of a Hexadecimal format mode.
Displays the value using binary format. Use the method to create an instance of a Binary format mode.
Displays the value using scientific notation format. Use the method to create an instance of a Scientific format mode.

remarks.para:
When formats a value, there are two different states that affect how the value is formatted: and . The state is passed into as a member of the argument.
indicates that the value will be used for display and indicates that the value will be used for editing. If the state is , all built-in format modes generate a fully formatted string representation of the value. If the state is , the format modes generate a formatted string representation of the value that can be parsed with . The SimpleDouble, Engineering, Hexadecimal, Binary, and Scientific modes generate the same formatted string representation for both display and editing. The Generic format mode generates a fully formatted string representation for display and a basic numeric string representation for editing.

For the built-in format modes, if the machine running the application that uses NumericFormatMode is configured so that symbols used to format numbers are more than one character wide, the method will return false for partially entered values. For example, in the NumericEdit control, the user might not be able to enter these formatting symbols into the control. Some examples of the formatting symbols included are the decimal symbol and the group separator symbol.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.Plot.SmoothUpdates
member.summary: Gets or sets the value which specifies whether the plot is drawn to an off-screen buffer before drawing to the screen.
member.value: if a plot is drawn to an off-screen buffer before drawing to the screen. The default value is .

remarks.para:
Smooth updating improves performance in the following ways:
Eliminates flashing associated with plotting large plots.
Optimizes speed when you use graph cursors.
Optimizes speed when a graph is redrawn after it has been overlapped or hidden.

Smooth updating has the following disadvantages:
Initial plotting speed is comparatively slower because the plot is first drawn to an off-screen buffer and then drawn to the screen.
Uses extra memory for the off-screen bitmap.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.RefreshItem.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.

remarks.para: creates a new object that is a deep copy of .

A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: P:NationalInstruments.UI.Scale.InteractionMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the user interactions that are supported by the scale.
member.value: A that indicates which user interactions are supported by the scale. The default value is .
member.exception: The specified value is not a value.

remarks.para: Set the Enabled property to on the control containing the scale to enable interaction with the scale. If the Enabled property is , the has no effect regardless of its value. Also, the scale must be visible in order for the to have any effect.

If is set to , a user can interactively set the minimum and maximum values of the scale at run time. If the minimum value is set to a value greater than or equal to the maximum value, then the maximum value is set to the value obtained by adding the new minimum value and the old range interval. The scale then appears to slide positively. Similarly, if the maximum value is set to a value less than the minimum value, then the minimum value is set to the value obtained by subtracting the old range interval from the new maximum value. The scale then appears to slide negatively.

For example, if the scale range is 10 to 30, the range interval is 30 - 10, or 20. If the minimum value of 10 is interactively changed to 30, then the maximum value is changed to 30 + 20, or 50. So the new range is 30 to 50. Similarly, given a scale range of 10 to 30, if you change the maximum value from 30 to 10 interactively, then the minimum value is changed to 10 - 20, or -10.

Displays the value using standard engineering notations supported by . Use the method to create an instance of an Engineering format mode.
Displays the value using hexadecimal format. Use the method to create an instance of a Hexadecimal format mode.
Displays the value using binary format. Use the method to create an instance of a Binary format mode.
Displays the value using scientific notation format. Use the method to create an instance of a Scientific format mode.

remarks.para: For more information, refer to the class.

member.summary: Creates a new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.remarks: A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.remarks:

Division tick marks are placed at values that fit the following equation:
Base + (n * )
where

member.remarks:
defines a class for plotting waveforms that represent x or y values. A waveform is a set of data plotted at specified increments.
Use and to pre-configure the start and increment values before plotting data.
plots a single x value or an array of x values against a starting y value using a value to increment y values. When you plot data, the value is ignored. With , you can explicitly specify the starting y value and the value to use to increment y values. If these values are not specified, the values of and are used. You can specify the starting y value as a or as a value. You can specify the value that increments the y values as a or as a value.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.WaveformPlot.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of with and set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.XAxis.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.remarks: A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.XYCursor.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a copy of this instance.
member.remarks:
creates a new object that is a deep copy of with set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

remarks.para: The class provides static methods for creating instances of the following common error data modes:

item.description: Generates no error data. Use the method to create an instance of a None error data mode.
Generates error data that is offset from plotted data points by a constant amount. Use the method to create an instance of a Constant error data mode.
Generates error data that is offset from plotted data points by a percentage of the values for the plotted data. Use the method to create an instance of a Percent error data mode.

remarks.para: The format of the string used to display symmetric error data modes in the designer is [mode name]: [symmetric offset], and the format used to display asymmetric error data modes in the designer is [mode name]: +[high offset], -[low offset].
remarks.note: When you implement a class that derives from , you must implement the method. You must also validate arguments of this method and handle invalid arguments appropriately.

You can customize the appearance of a point annotation in many ways. Use the , , , , , and properties to change the color and style of the fill area as well as the color, width, and style of the bounding line. Use the property to completely hide all parts of the annotation when the point of interest is not located inside the plot area bounds.

creates a new object that is a deep copy of the with the and set to .
A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.

member.name: M:NationalInstruments.UI.YAxis.Clone
member.summary: Creates a new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.returns: A new object that is a deep copy of this instance.
member.remarks: A shallow copy creates a new instance of the same type as the original object, and then copies the nonstatic fields of the original object. If the field is a value type, a bit-by-bit copy of the field is performed. If the field is a reference type, the reference is copied but the referred object is not; therefore, the reference in the original object and the reference in the clone point to the same object. In contrast, a deep copy of an object duplicates everything directly or indirectly referenced by the fields in the object.
